A2 (2026-10-09, reviewer-requested re-audit): all 37 records coded representation_only_ablation were re-judged at full text by two independent checkers (Claude agents, isoaudit_out/; GPT via codex, stage3_extraction/isoaudit2/out/) under a sharper four-level rule (R-strict / R-unmatched-budget / component / not-isolated); cleanest comparison per paper counts. 27/37 agreed; the authors decided the 10 disagreements (isoaudit2/human_decisions.json). The evaluation level representation_only_ablation is replaced by repr_strict (7), repr_unmatched_budget (13), component_ablation (15); not-isolated (2) -> ablated_measured. Seven extraction errors fixed and six primary-study inconsistencies recorded (apply_adjudications.py section 1b). Applied deterministically by apply_adjudications.py section 3.
boundary_rules_added: B1: pre-trained transformer code-LMs (CodeBERT/GraphCodeBERT/UniXcoder family) count as language models when the record's CONTRIBUTION is a structural representation or context mechanism for the LM (integration point: fine-tuning); GNN-primary fusions where the neural-graph model does the detection are E2.
B2: training-method papers (RL/GRPO, instruction tuning) with no structural representation in the input fail E1 — the map is about what grounds the model, not how it is optimized.

B3: empirical studies that VARY context or code surface form (context-window length, prompt scope, obfuscation transforms, project-scale context) are in scope as representation/context-effect studies (I2, second clause).
B4: malicious-code/skill detection via code analysis is in scope (I1); attacks ON agent loops remain E3.
